answer: For an acute cough (less than 3 weeks), if it does not resolve on its own, further evaluation is needed only when the cough lasts more than 8 weeks. [ACCP Clinical Practice Guideline, 2006] Persistent cough beyond this duration should be evaluated for underlying conditions such as asthma, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), or post-nasal drip. If you encounter a persistent cough lasting over 8 weeks, consider consulting a healthcare professional for further evaluation. [ACCP Clinical Practice Guideline, 2006]

results.content: Acute cough (under 3 weeks) is most often due to a viral upper respiratory infection and resolves without treatment; over-the-counter cough suppressants provide modest symptom relief. A cough lasting more than 8 weeks is chronic and warrants evaluation for causes such as asthma, GERD, or post-nasal drip.
results.citation: Diagnosis and Management of Cough, American College of Chest Physicians, 2006
